page.layout: One page of text, running head at the top, page number at the top right, catchword at the foot on the right. No marginal notes.

l.i: Si salute mea, & prosperis haud delectaris, en me
promptum in quodcunque de me vis fieri, cujus
sepè Iudicia à Filiis tuis ordiuntur.
Ipse nihil fiam ut Tu sis omnia.
Tu me docuisti Nullum Regem salvari multitudi-
ne Exercitus, Tu me potes servare Misericordia-
rum Tuarum Multitudine qui es Dominus
Exercituum & Misericordiarum Pater.
Subvenias mihi Domine undequaque oppres-
so[?], Tu meas partes suscipias, & non timebo quid
faciat mihi Caro.
Gloriam tuæ Iustitiæ in Adversis Meis, a-
gnosco. O glorificet se Tua Misericordia in libe-
rando Me ab iis qui Animam meam persequun-
tur.
Per peccata mea contra Te pugnavi, Tuus sub-
ditus, & Te Gloria Tua Spoliavi, jure ergo Tu
optimo potes Me per subditos meos & spoliare Ro-
bore meo, & obscurare Gloriam.
Quin Te Monstres spes mea, & unicum Per-
fugium: Ne dicant Inimici mei, non est salus Ipse
in Deo ejus.
Perfice greffus meos in semitis Tuis ut non mo-
veantur vestigia mea, ne nutent pedes mei.
Custodi me ut pupillam oculi, sub umbra ala-
rum tuarum protege me.
Infigniter ostende Bonitatem Tuam, tu qui ser-
vas dextra tua sperantes in Te, à resistentibus
Dexterae Tuae.
Ab Impiis hominibus qui me opprimunt, & ab
Inimicis, qui animam Meam circumdederunt.

page.notes: Running head and title are Greek (ΕΙΚΩΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΚΗ as printed, EIKΩN BAΣIΛIKH.). The italic/roman split within lines is approximate: capitalised names such as Nullum Regem and Dominus look roman. Doubtful readings: "sepè" (scan reads "fepè"), "oppres-so[?]" (word broken at line end, second syllable hard to read), "Monstres" as printed. A small dot or asterisk mark stands after "protege me." in the line of "Custodi me"; it may be a printer's mark and is not transcribed as text. Small mark at the bottom centre of the page is not text and is omitted. Printed spacing "Tuussub-ditus" and "Tuam,tu" is read as "Tuus sub-ditus" and "Tuam, tu".
